skill.name: nowait-reasoning-optimizer
skill.description: Applies the NOWAIT technique to reduce reflection tokens in R1-style reasoning models. Use it to configure token suppression for HuggingFace and vLLM inference workflows.
skill.summary: Reduce repeated reflection tokens in reasoning model inference with NOWAIT.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Reasoning models can spend many tokens on repeated reflection. This skill applies NOWAIT guidance to suppress selected reflection tokens during inference.
actual_capabilities: Provides a NOWAIT logit processor for HuggingFace generation workflows.
Builds suppressed token IDs from tokenizer vocabulary and keyword matches.
Returns bad words ID lists for vLLM-style generation settings.
Includes default reflection keywords and excluded false-positive patterns.
Offers a stopping criteria option for limiting reflection markers.
Documents model families where NOWAIT performs better or worse.
limitations: Does not train, fine-tune, or evaluate a model by itself.
May reduce accuracy on distilled reasoning models and difficult tasks.
Requires access to a tokenizer and generation pipeline.
Token savings depend on model family, prompts, and keyword tuning.

use_cases.title: Integrate token suppression
use_cases.description: Add keyword-based suppression to HuggingFace or vLLM generation settings.

output_examples.input: Review whether QwQ-32B is suitable for NOWAIT.
output_examples.output: QwQ-32B is a strong fit. Start with the default keyword list, then compare token counts and accuracy on representative prompts.

output_examples.input: Plan a NOWAIT evaluation for visual question answering.
output_examples.output: Use paired runs with and without suppression. Track output quality, token count, latency, and failures on hard visual reasoning questions.

output_examples.input: Decide whether to use NOWAIT on a distilled model.
output_examples.output: Use caution. Distilled models may rely on reflection structure, so require accuracy testing before enabling suppression.

best_practices: Benchmark token savings and answer quality before production use.
Tune keywords per model family instead of assuming one list fits all models.
Keep a fallback path that disables suppression when accuracy drops.
anti_patterns: Do not enable NOWAIT on distilled models without task-specific evaluation.
Do not suppress broad words when they are required by the task domain.
Do not judge success by token reduction without checking answer quality.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It helps reduce repeated reflection tokens during reasoning model inference.

faq.question: Does it work with every model?
faq.answer: No. It works best with supported RL-based reasoning models and needs testing on each workload.

faq.question: Does it change model weights?
faq.answer: No. NOWAIT is an inference-time technique and does not fine-tune the model.

faq.question: Can it improve latency?
faq.answer: It can reduce generated tokens, which may lower latency when quality remains stable.

faq.question: What should I test first?
faq.answer: Compare baseline and NOWAIT outputs on representative prompts, accuracy metrics, token counts, and failure cases.

faq.question: Is it safe for production?
faq.answer: Use it only after evaluation confirms acceptable accuracy, monitoring, and a clear rollback path.
